figures.alt: A router sends one token state to two of eight parallel feedforward experts. Router weights scale the two expert outputs before they are summed.
figures.caption: One token, two selected FFN experts. Reproduced from Jiang et al., Figure 1; figure crop, CC BY 4.0.
figures.purpose: Follow the two solid branches in Figure 1: the experts receive the same token state and run in parallel, not one after the other. The dotted path supplies mixing weights. Attention and the surrounding decoder remain shared; routing replaces the FFN sublayer.

figures.alt: Across Pile domains and decoder layers, consecutive tokens often reuse the first-choice expert or overlap in either of their top-two experts; dashed lines show uniform independent routing baselines.
figures.caption: Consecutive tokens often reuse experts. Reproduced from Jiang et al., Figure 10; figure crop, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
figures.purpose: The upper panel of Figure 2 asks whether the first-choice expert repeats. The lower panel asks whether either expert overlaps between adjacent top-two sets. They have different random baselines, so their heights are not directly comparable. Domain labels describe the sampled texts, not experts with fixed subject assignments.[^report]
